title: Sabrina Setup Wizard
intro: Install Sabrina, the chief-of-staff agent, on one Google account. About 20 to 30 steps. You enter each value once. The wizard reuses it in later steps. The last part is the installation test.

variables.label: Client or business name
variables.help: Used in names and labels only.

variables.label: Owner email
variables.help: The Google account that runs Sabrina. Gmail or Google Workspace. Not Microsoft 365.

variables.label: Email domain
variables.help: The part after the @ in the owner email.
variables.pattern_error: Enter the domain only, for example yourdomain.com.

variables.label: Time zone (IANA name)
variables.help: Nudges, deadlines and the overnight window all use this time zone.
variables.pattern_error: Use the IANA name, for example America/Chicago.

variables.label: Sabrina's sending address
variables.help: Worked out for you from your domain. Change it only if you want a different name.

variables.label: Other addresses that may start a job
variables.help: Optional. One address, or several separated by commas. Every address you send from must be here.

variables.label: Job Board Sheet ID
variables.help: The long ID in the Sheet address bar, between /d/ and /edit.
variables.pattern_error: This does not look like a Sheet ID.

variables.label: Task Calendar name
variables.help: Keep the default unless the client already has a calendar for this.

variables.label: Task Calendar ID
variables.help: Calendar settings, Integrate calendar, Calendar ID.

variables.label: Client Update template doc ID
variables.help: The long ID in the doc address bar, between /d/ and /edit.
variables.pattern_error: This does not look like a doc ID.

variables.label: Lane 1
variables.help: A lane is one area of work. Use short names. Each lane also becomes a Gmail label.
variables.pattern_error: Use 2 to 40 characters. No quote marks.

variables.label: Lane 2
variables.pattern_error: Use 2 to 40 characters. No quote marks.

variables.label: Lane 3
variables.pattern_error: Use 2 to 40 characters. No quote marks.

variables.label: Lane 4
variables.pattern_error: Use 2 to 40 characters. No quote marks.

variables.label: Lane 5
variables.pattern_error: Use 2 to 40 characters. No quote marks.

variables.label: Lane 6
variables.pattern_error: Use 2 to 40 characters. No quote marks.

variables.label: Lane for your own domain
variables.help: Mail to or from your own domain goes to this lane when no label says otherwise. Type the lane name exactly.

variables.label: Dashboard web app URL
variables.help: You get this in the dashboard step.

variables.label: Meeting note-taker
variables.help: Optional. Gemini notes need no extra setup. Any other tool needs one extra step.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.instructions:
You need five things.
1. A Gmail or Google Workspace account. Not Microsoft 365.
2. A Claude plan that has Cowork.
3. Three template links from ReRev Labs: the Job Board, the Apps Script project, and the Client Update doc.
4. About 30 minutes for the install and 30 more for the test.
5. A second browser tab for this wizard.

Enter the values below. The wizard keeps them in this browser only.
steps.checkbox_label: I have the account, the Cowork plan and the three links
steps.verify_hint: All seven fields show no red message.

steps.title: Create Sabrina's sending address
steps.instructions:
Sabrina sends every email from her own address. Make it an alias on {{owner_email}}.

1. Open Gmail.
2. Open Settings, then See all settings, then Accounts and Import.
3. Next to Send mail as, choose Add another email address.
4. Enter {{agent_alias}}. Keep Treat as an alias on.
5. Confirm the address.

On Google Workspace, an admin may first need to add the alias to the user in the Admin console.
steps.checkbox_label: The alias is confirmed
steps.verify_hint: {{agent_alias}} appears under Send mail as with no Verify link next to it.

steps.title: Copy the Job Board
steps.instructions:
The Job Board is Sabrina's only memory. Copy it first. You need its real ID before the script step.

1. Open {{job_board_template_url}}.
2. Choose File, then Make a copy.
3. Name the copy 'Sabrina - Job Board - {{client_name}}'.
4. Save it in {{owner_email}}'s Drive.
5. Copy the Sheet ID from the address bar of the new copy.
steps.checkbox_label: I copied the Sheet and saved its ID
steps.verify_hint: The copy has five tabs: jobs, history, deliverables, attachments, projects. The jobs tab has 17 columns in row 1. Column 15 is time_estimate, column 16 is run_after and column 17 is lane. If your copy has a column named due_at, or the order differs, stop and ask ReRev Labs for a fresh template.

steps.title: Create the Task Calendar
steps.instructions:
Sabrina reads events from one calendar that only holds her tasks. Keep it apart from real events.

1. Open Google Calendar on {{owner_email}}.
2. Next to Other calendars, choose Add, then Create new calendar.
3. Name it {{calendar_name}}.
4. Open the calendar's settings.
5. Under Integrate calendar, copy the Calendar ID.
steps.checkbox_label: The calendar exists and I saved its ID
steps.verify_hint: The Calendar ID ends in @group.calendar.google.com.

steps.title: Copy the Client Update doc template
steps.instructions:
Each client gets one living Client Update doc. This is the template for it.

1. Open {{update_template_url}}.
2. Choose File, then Make a copy.
3. Name it 'Client Update Template'.
4. Do not share it with anyone. The doc is client-visible later, so Sabrina asks before she shares it.
5. Copy the doc ID from the address bar.
steps.checkbox_label: The template is copied, private, and I saved its ID
steps.verify_hint: The sharing button shows Restricted.

steps.title: Copy the Apps Script project
steps.instructions:
1. Open {{script_template_url}}.
2. Choose the Overview page, then Make a copy.
3. Open the copy. It lives in {{owner_email}}'s Drive.
4. Name it 'Sabrina - Task Agent'.
5. Open Project Settings. Turn on Show appsscript.json manifest file.
6. Open appsscript.json. Set the time zone line as shown below.
7. Save.

The script reads its time zone from this file. If it is wrong, deadlines, nudges and the overnight window all run at the wrong hour.

If the project has a file named QueueCourses, delete that file. It is a one-off for ReRev Labs.
steps.checkbox_label: The project is copied and the time zone is set
steps.verify_hint: The file list shows 13 files: appsscript, Code, Followup, SmokeTest, Email, Attachments, DeadLetter, Lanes, DashboardData, DashboardHtml, Bounce, Addon, AddonHome. No QueueCourses.

steps.title: Set the identifiers in Code.gs
steps.instructions:
Open Code.gs. Find the block that starts with const CFG. Replace the values with the ones below.

This step edits code. Edit only the lines shown. Leave PRIORITY_LANES empty.

Also open SmokeTest.gs. Find SMOKE_DOC_ID. Replace its value with the Client Update template doc ID.

copy.label: Code.gs, ALLOWLIST

steps.checkbox_label: CFG and SMOKE_DOC_ID are set and saved
steps.verify_hint: No line in CFG still shows the ReRev Labs sheet, calendar, or email values. The DASHBOARD_URL line is empty for now.

steps.title: Set the lanes in Lanes.gs
steps.instructions:
A lane is one area of work. Sabrina tags every job with a lane. The Dashboard groups work by lane.

The lane names are in the code. If you skip this step, the Dashboard shows another business's lanes on your data.

In Lanes.gs, replace these four items: LANE_CANON, LANE_GROUPS, LANE_ALIASES and LANE_DOMAINS. Use the blocks below. Delete any line that still shows a name in angle brackets.

LANE_GROUPS stays empty. Every lane then stands alone.
steps.checkbox_label: The four lane items are replaced and saved
steps.verify_hint: Search Lanes.gs for the previous owner's lane names. None remain in these four items.

steps.title: Create the Gmail labels
steps.instructions:
Create these labels in Gmail on {{owner_email}}.

1. Agent. This is the trigger label. Name it exactly Agent.
2. One label per lane. Each name must match the lane name exactly.

A label that matches a lane name tells Sabrina which lane a thread belongs to. Skip any line that shows a name in angle brackets.
steps.checkbox_label: The Agent label and the lane labels exist
steps.verify_hint: The label list shows Agent and each lane name.

steps.title: Authorize the script and send the first test email
steps.instructions:
1. In the Apps Script editor, pick selfTest in the function list.
2. Choose Run.
3. Google asks for permission. Choose Review permissions.
4. Choose your account. Choose Advanced, then Go to the project. Choose Allow.
5. Run selfTest again if the first run stopped at the permission screen.

The warning screen is normal. The script is yours. It is not published.

The script asks for mail, calendar, Drive, Sheets and Gmail add-on access. Sabrina needs all of them.
steps.checkbox_label: selfTest ran with no error
steps.verify_hint: An email arrives in {{owner_email}} from {{agent_alias}}. The subject starts with [5 min]. If no email arrives, open Executions in the editor and read the error.

steps.title: Deploy the Dashboard
steps.instructions:
The Dashboard is a web page that shows all work by lane. Every Sabrina email links to it.

1. In the editor, choose Deploy, then New deployment.
2. Choose type Web app.
3. Description: Sabrina Dashboard v1.
4. Execute as: Me.
5. Who has access: Only myself.
6. Choose Deploy.
7. Copy the Web app URL. It ends in /exec.
8. Paste it below.
9. Put the same URL in CFG, in the DASHBOARD_URL line. Save.

Keep the deployment name the same on every install. After any code change, use Deploy, then Manage deployments, then Edit, then New version. A new deployment makes a new URL.
steps.checkbox_label: The Dashboard is deployed and the URL is in CFG
steps.verify_hint: Open {{dashboard_url}}. The page loads and shows your lane names. It shows no ReRev Labs lanes.

steps.title: Install the Gmail add-on
steps.instructions:
The add-on puts Sabrina in the Gmail side panel. You can hand an email to her, answer her, and close jobs with buttons.

1. In the editor, choose Deploy, then Test deployments.
2. Next to Application type, choose Gmail add-on. Choose Install.
3. Reload Gmail.
4. Look for the Sabrina icon in the right side panel. Open it.

A test deployment installs for the account that runs it. Each person who wants the panel must install it from their own copy.
steps.checkbox_label: The Sabrina panel shows in Gmail
steps.verify_hint: The panel shows 'Right now' with four numbers and a Dashboard button. Open any email. The panel shows a form with a Send to Sabrina button.

steps.title: Turn on the timers
steps.instructions:
Do this only after the first test email arrived.

1. In the editor, pick installTriggers in the function list.
2. Choose Run.
3. Open Triggers (the clock icon).

The function deletes any existing triggers first. Run it once. Run it again after you add a trigger.
steps.checkbox_label: The 8 triggers are listed
steps.verify_hint: Triggers shows 8 rows: watchCalendar every 15 minutes, watchGmailLabel every 5, sendPending every 5, watchReplies every 5, watchdog every hour, verifyDeliverables every 2 hours, nudgeSweep daily near 9am, releaseHeavyJobs every 15 minutes.

steps.title: Send mail to the alias into Sabrina
steps.instructions:
Mail sent or forwarded to {{agent_alias}} must get the Agent label. A Gmail filter does this. Make it on the main account first. Each extra inbox sends work to Sabrina by email too. It does not get its own script.

On the main account, then on each extra account:
1. Open Gmail settings, then Filters and Blocked Addresses.
2. Create a filter. In To, enter {{agent_alias}}.
3. Choose Apply the label, and pick Agent.

Then add each extra account's sending address to ALLOWLIST in Code.gs. Sabrina reads only the main mailbox. A job from another inbox cannot be checked automatically. Its deliverables must be type manual.
steps.checkbox_label: The filter exists on the main account and on each extra inbox
steps.verify_hint: Every sending address is in ALLOWLIST. The main account and every extra inbox have the filter.

steps.title: Choose the meeting note-taker
steps.instructions:
After a call, Sabrina reads the transcript. Google Meet with Gemini notes works with no extra setup.

Any other note-taker needs one extra step. A function in the same Apps Script must land its transcripts in one Drive folder. Ask ReRev Labs for that step before the test.

Decide now. The meeting test needs a real transcript.
steps.checkbox_label: The note-taker is decided
steps.verify_hint: Write the tool name above. If it is not Gemini notes, tell ReRev Labs.

steps.title: Connect Cowork
steps.instructions:
Cowork is the worker. It claims a job, does the work, and writes the result on the Job Board.

In Cowork, connect these four connectors to {{owner_email}}:
1. Google Drive
2. Google Docs
3. Google Calendar
4. Google Sheets

Sheets holds the Job Board. Drive and Docs hold the Client Update docs. Calendar holds the meeting invites.
steps.checkbox_label: All four connectors are connected
steps.verify_hint: The Connectors screen shows four Google connectors, all connected.

steps.title: Set up the Cowork skill
steps.instructions:
The skill holds the rules Cowork follows on every run.

1. Open the Cowork runtime skill template from ReRev Labs.
2. Open the identifiers table in the skill. Replace each value with the ones below.
3. Compress the skill folder into one zip file.
4. In Claude, open Settings, then Customize, then Skills.
5. Upload the zip.

Claude takes a zip. It does not take a folder.

copy.label: Values for the skill identifiers table

steps.checkbox_label: The skill is uploaded
steps.verify_hint: The skill shows in Settings, Customize, Skills. No ReRev Labs ID is left in the table.

steps.title: Create the Cowork scheduled task
steps.instructions:
1. In Cowork, create a scheduled task.
2. Cadence: hourly.
3. Status: Active.
4. Point it at the Sabrina runtime skill.
5. Keep the prompt to three lines. The skill holds the rules.

Start hourly. Make it faster only after the full test passes.
steps.checkbox_label: The task is Active and hourly
steps.verify_hint: The scheduled tasks list shows the task as Active with an hourly cadence.

steps.title: TEST 1: The first email
steps.instructions:
This checks the Google side with no agent involved.

1. Run selfTest again.
2. Open the email from {{agent_alias}}.

Check each item:
1. The subject starts with [5 min] and ends with a job ID in brackets.
2. The email has blocks: what I know, end goal, deliverables, direction, why, to start.
3. The footer shows a Dashboard button and a Job Board link.
4. Both links open.
5. The job row shows on the jobs tab, and the history tab shows a Sent email entry.
steps.checkbox_label: All five checks pass
steps.verify_hint: If the footer has no Dashboard button, CFG.DASHBOARD_URL is empty. Fix it, save, and run again.

steps.title: TEST 2: Follow-up and verification
steps.instructions:
This proves nudges and deliverable checks in ten minutes. You do not wait two days.

Run these in the editor, in order:
1. smokeTestSetup. An email arrives. The board has a test job with two deliverables.
2. verifyDeliverables. Deliverable d1 changes to verified.
3. smokeTestNudge. A nudge arrives as a reply on the same thread.
4. smokeTestCleanup. The test job closes.

nudgeSweep does nothing on Saturday and Sunday. Run this test on a weekday.
steps.checkbox_label: Setup, verify, nudge and cleanup all worked
steps.verify_hint: In the deliverables tab, d1 is verified and d2 is waived after cleanup.

steps.title: TEST 3: Cowork smoke test
steps.instructions:
Open a Cowork chat that has the Sabrina skill. Ask it to do these three things.
1. Read one cell on the Job Board.
2. Write one cell on the Job Board.
3. Answer a question that only your account memory can answer. Use something that is not in the Sheet or Calendar, for example a saved writing-style preference.

If Cowork can read but cannot write, stop. The design needs both.
steps.checkbox_label: Cowork read, wrote and answered from memory
steps.verify_hint: Open the Sheet. The cell you asked Cowork to write now holds the new value. Clear it afterward.

steps.title: TEST 4: Calendar to email
steps.instructions:
1. On the Task Calendar, create an event. Start its title with [Agent]. Example: [Agent] Draft a thank-you note. Put one line in the description: Lane: {{lane1}}.
2. Wait up to 15 minutes. A new row appears on the jobs tab with status queued.
3. Wait for the next hourly Cowork run. The row changes to claimed, then awaiting_human.
4. An email arrives from {{agent_alias}}.

Check:
1. The queued row has the lane in column 17.
2. Cowork claimed the row. The history tab shows a claim entry.
3. The email is short. It fits one phone screen.
4. The subject has a time tag when Cowork could estimate your time.
5. The email footer shows an In play list for the lane.
steps.checkbox_label: The event became a job, and an email arrived
steps.verify_hint: Calendar watcher runs every 15 minutes. Cowork runs hourly. The whole path can take up to 75 minutes.

steps.title: TEST 5: Inbound email and the allowlist
steps.instructions:
Test the path in, separate from send-as.

1. From {{owner_email}}, send an email to {{agent_alias}}. Subject: Test inbound. Body: Please draft a one-line reply to this.
2. Gmail applies the Agent label (your filter does this).
3. Within 5 minutes a new job row appears with job_class email.

Now test the guard.
4. From an address that is not on ALLOWLIST, send one email to {{agent_alias}}.
5. You get a rejected-message notice. The label is removed. No job starts.
steps.checkbox_label: The alias receives mail, and a stranger is rejected
steps.verify_hint: If the first email never arrives, the alias does not receive mail. Check the alias setup in Workspace.

steps.title: TEST 6: Gmail add-on
steps.instructions:
1. Open any email that is not from Sabrina.
2. Open the Sabrina panel.
3. Write a direction. Choose a lane. Choose Send to Sabrina.
4. A notice says Sent to Sabrina, with a job ID.
5. The panel now shows a job card with status and buttons.
6. Choose Snooze 2d. The card confirms.
7. Open the panel home. It shows 'Right now' with four numbers.

Check that a button and a typed reply do the same thing. Reply close to the job's email thread, on another job. It closes the same way.
steps.checkbox_label: The panel sent a job and the buttons worked
steps.verify_hint: The jobs tab shows the new row with the lane you chose in column 17, and the history tab shows 'Direction from Gmail add-on'.

steps.title: TEST 7: Dashboard and lanes
steps.instructions:
1. Open {{dashboard_url}}.
2. The KPI row shows counts.
3. The lane list shows your lanes: {{lane1}}, {{lane2}}.
4. It shows no lane names from another business.
5. Open a lane. Its items show.
6. Find the job from Test 4. It sits in {{lane1}}.

Now test the Gmail label route.
7. Put the label {{lane2}} on an email in your inbox.
8. Send that email to {{agent_alias}}.
9. The new job's lane is {{lane2}}.
steps.checkbox_label: The Dashboard shows my lanes and the lane routes work
steps.verify_hint: A lane that resolves wrong usually means a label name that does not match the lane name exactly.

steps.title: TEST 8: Attachments
steps.instructions:
Cowork cannot read Gmail attachments. The script copies them to Drive.

1. Forward an email that has a PDF to {{agent_alias}}.
2. Wait for the job row.
3. Open Drive. Find the folder 'Task Agent - Attachments'. Open the folder for the new job.
4. The PDF is there.
5. Open the attachments tab on the Sheet. One row names the file and a read_with value.
steps.checkbox_label: The PDF is in Drive and on the attachments tab
steps.verify_hint: Small logos, calendar invites, and files over 25 MB are skipped by design.

steps.title: TEST 9: Reply verbs and the overnight window
steps.instructions:
Use the email from any open job. Reply with one word or phrase at a time. Check the Sheet after each.

1. snooze 2d. The nudge_after cell moves two days out.
2. waiting on Test Person. The status changes to awaiting_external.
3. heavy. The status changes to scheduled. The run_after cell holds a time at or after 10pm in {{timezone}}. If it is already between 10pm and 4am, it holds the current time.
4. run now. The status returns to queued and run_after clears.
5. close. The status changes to done.

The 10pm to 4am window uses the script time zone. If run_after shows the wrong hour, fix appsscript.json.
steps.checkbox_label: All five verbs worked and run_after is correct
steps.verify_hint: Each verb adds a keyona entry on the history tab.

steps.title: TEST 10: Nothing dies quietly
steps.instructions:
Two guards stop a job from sitting unseen.

Guard 1, dead letters.
1. On the jobs tab, add a test row. Set status to failed. Leave pending_email empty.
2. In the editor, run inspectDeadLetters. It lists the row. It changes nothing.
3. Wait for the next hourly watchdog. An email arrives for that row. The row moves to awaiting_human.

Guard 2, silent parking.
4. Add a test row. Set status to awaiting_human. Leave pending_email empty.
5. Wait 30 minutes plus one sendPending run. The row returns to queued.

Delete both test rows after.
steps.checkbox_label: Both guards caught the test rows
steps.verify_hint: The history tab has a script entry for each row.

steps.title: TEST 11: A real call
steps.instructions:
Run one real call transcript through the meeting flow.

1. Hold a short call with a recurring invite. Use the note-taker you chose: {{note_taker}}.
2. After the call, wait for the next Cowork run.
3. The board shows one meeting_item row for each action item that belongs to the owner.
4. Items Claude can do are queued. Items that need the owner are awaiting_human, each with an email.
5. The client's Client Update doc now exists. It is still private.
6. An approval ticket asks the owner to reply yes to share it.
7. Reply yes. The doc attaches to the recurring invite.
8. The client got no calendar or share email you did not expect.

Sabrina sends no recap. Google already sends one.
steps.checkbox_label: The meeting flow passed all eight checks
steps.verify_hint: Open the doc's sharing settings before you reply yes. It must show Restricted.

steps.title: Done: record this install
steps.instructions:
The install is complete when every test box is checked.

1. Choose Copy my values at the top of this page.
2. Email the values to ReRev Labs. They log the install and its version.
3. Keep the Job Board and the Apps Script project. The Apps Script copy is the only place your code runs.

Needs a human, not covered by this test: the Idea Nurture flow, the build class, and the deadline-tag email. Test them when you first use them.
steps.checkbox_label: I sent my values to ReRev Labs
steps.verify_hint: ReRev Labs confirms the install is logged.
